facts.fact_text: On 14 June 2008 a group called the 'Che Guevara Fan Club' held a gathering at a private café in Baku to celebrate the eightieth anniversary of the birth of Che Guevara.
The café where the gathering was held on 14 June 2008 was located in the basement of a building in the city centre of Baku.
There were about twenty-five attendees at the gathering held by the 'Che Guevara Fan Club' on 14 June 2008.
The applicant attended the gathering held by the 'Che Guevara Fan Club' on 14 June 2008, accompanied by two colleagues from the Institute for Reporters' Freedom and Safety (IRFS), R.A. and M.H.
The gathering held by the 'Che Guevara Fan Club' on 14 June 2008 began at noon.
Article 49 of the Constitution of the Republic of Azerbaijan provides that everyone has the right to freely assemble together with others.

Article 49 of the Constitution of the Republic of Azerbaijan provides that everyone has the right, upon notification to relevant Government bodies in advance, to assemble peacefully with others, without arms, and to hold rallies, meetings, demonstrations, street marches and pickets.

Article 4.1 of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 of Azerbaijan, as in force at the material time, provided that the right to hold gatherings in places which are in private ownership is not regulated by that Law.

Article 7 of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 of Azerbaijan provides that any restriction on freedom of assembly may be put in place only by law and for the purposes of protecting interests necessary in a democratic society, including: protection of the interests of public and state security; preventing the disturbance of public order; prevention of disorder or crime; protection of the health of the population; protection of morals; and protection of the rights and freedoms of others.

The Venice Commission Opinion no. 384/2006 stated that Article 4.1 of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 of Azerbaijan, which provides that peaceful assemblies in places in private ownership shall not be regulated by the Law, is positive in that assemblies on private property are exempted from any notification requirement as well as from all other requirements provided for in the Law.

The Venice Commission Opinion no. 384/2006 stated that Article 4.1 of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 of Azerbaijan shall not be interpreted as prohibiting spontaneous assemblies on private property, and that if the assembly is peaceful it should be allowed.
Approximately thirty minutes after the gathering began on 14 June 2008, about thirty police officers entered the café.
Some of the police officers who entered the café on 14 June 2008 were in police uniform and others were in plain clothes.
The police officers who entered the café on 14 June 2008 suspended the gathering and announced that they were going to take the attendees to the police station.

In response to the applicant's actions, one of the police officers, who was apparently in charge of the intervention on 14 June 2008, ordered other police officers to take the applicant to the police station.
According to the applicant, he was taken to a police car by four police officers on 14 June 2008, who used force against him.
According to the applicant, the four police officers who took him to the police car on 14 June 2008 punched and kicked him in the stomach.

According to the Government, on 14 June 2008 the police intervened in the gathering at the café on the basis of a complaint from people living in the neighbourhood of the café, who complained about noise and the behaviour of those attending.

According to the Government, the applicant and other attendees who were unable to produce their identity cards were taken to the police station but were released once their identity had been established.

The spokesman for the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Azerbaijan, E.Z., stated that on 14 June 2008 a group of people held an unauthorised gathering at a café and the police requested the interruption of the unauthorised gathering.

The spokesman for the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Azerbaijan, E.Z., stated that twenty people were taken to Nasimi District Police Station no. 22 in order to establish their identity and to conduct the relevant explanatory interviews (izahat işləri), and that they were all released following the explanatory interviews.

The explanation issued by Nasimi District Police Station no. 22 on 25 June 2008 stated that on 14 June 2008, at around 1 p.m., police officers from the Baku City Police Office took measures to identify persons gathered at café 'Alaturka' in the basement of building no. 6 at 28 May Street in Baku, and twenty-two of them were taken to Nasimi District Police Station no. 22.

The explanation issued by Nasimi District Police Station no. 22 on 25 June 2008 stated that after the individuals arrived at Nasimi District Police Station no. 22 at 1.55 p.m., they were registered in the 'apprehended persons' registration log' (gətirilmiş şəxslərin qeydiyyat kitabı) and were released at 4.30 p.m.

The explanation issued by Nasimi District Police Station no. 22 on 25 June 2008 stated that statements were taken from nine of the twenty-two individuals in order to establish the purpose of their gathering.

The explanation issued by Nasimi District Police Station no. 22 on 25 June 2008 stated that the individuals' identity was established and they were released following a 'prophylactic conversation' (profilaktik söhbət).

The explanation issued by Nasimi District Police Station no. 22 on 25 June 2008 stated that Huseynov Emin Rafik oglu, who presented a document stating that he was the chairman of the Institute for Reporters' Freedom and Safety (IRFS), was among the persons apprehended.

In his criminal complaint to the Nasimi District Court, the applicant complained that he had been unlawfully deprived of his liberty and that the police intervention of 14 June 2008 had been unlawful and had constituted an unjustified interference with his rights to freedom of expression and assembly.

In his civil action against the Nasimi District Police Office, the applicant, relying on Articles 3, 5, 10 and 11 of the Convention, complained that he had been ill-treated by the police, that he had been arrested and taken to the police station unlawfully, and that the police intervention in the gathering had constituted an unlawful interference with his rights to freedom of expression and assembly.
The Nasimi District Court's judgment of 17 June 2009 found that the applicant had been taken to the police station because he had not had his identity card on him.
The Nasimi District Court's judgment of 17 June 2009 found that the police intervention had been lawful, since the gathering at the café in the city centre disturbed other people present.

Article 14 of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 of Azerbaijan sets out the powers and duties of the police in connection with the holding of an assembly.

According to Article 14.I.3 of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 of Azerbaijan, the police have the right to suspend an assembly, if necessary, when the conduct of the assembly does not satisfy the conditions provided in the prior written notification.

Article 14.6 of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 of Azerbaijan provides that use of physical force or special equipment by the police should in all circumstances be proportional to the danger in question.

A criminal inquiry was launched by Nasimi District Police Station no. 22 in connection with information about the applicant's admission to the Clinical Medical Centre with injuries.
On 15 June 2008 the applicant was questioned in hospital by an investigator from Nasimi District Police Station no. 22.
The applicant described in detail to the investigator the circumstances of his arrest and detention by the police on 14 June 2008.

The applicant stated to the investigator that on 14 June 2008 he had attended the gathering commemorating the eightieth anniversary of the birth of Che Guevara, which had been interrupted by a police intervention.

The applicant stated to the investigator that when he protested about the arrest of his journalist colleagues on the orders of the police officer apparently in charge of the intervention, four police officers forcibly took him to a police car.
The applicant stated to the investigator that following his arrival at Nasimi District Police Station no. 22, he was taken to the room of the Deputy Head of the police station.

The applicant stated to the investigator that other police officers were also in the room of the Deputy Head of Nasimi District Police Station no. 22 and one of them, who was wearing black sunglasses, began insulting him and then threatening him, took out his gun and shouted at him.

The applicant stated to the investigator that the same police officer who was wearing black sunglasses struck him in the neck, as a result of which he lost consciousness, and that the police officers then took him out of the room.

On 17 June 2008, while the criminal inquiry was still pending, the spokesman for the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Azerbaijan, E.Z., gave an interview to the Turan Information Agency concerning the applicant's arrest and alleged ill-treatment by the police.

The spokesman for the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Azerbaijan, E.Z., stated in the interview that the statements made to the media by the applicant, Emin Huseynov, alleging that he was subjected to duress by the police were not true.
The spokesman for the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Azerbaijan, E.Z., stated that even the allegations published in the media were contradictory.

The spokesman for the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Azerbaijan, E.Z., stated that on 14 June 2008 a group of people held an unauthorised gathering at a café and the police requested the interruption of the unauthorised gathering.

The spokesman for the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Azerbaijan, E.Z., stated that twenty people were taken to Nasimi District Police Station no. 22 in order to establish their identity and to conduct the relevant explanatory interviews (izahat işləri), and that they were all released following the explanatory interviews.
The spokesman for the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Azerbaijan, E.Z., stated that Emin Huseynov said he did not feel well at the police station and an ambulance was called immediately.

The spokesman for the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Azerbaijan, E.Z., stated that it was established during the medical examination that Emin Huseynov's health problem was related to his previous diseases and that he had lost consciousness because his blood pressure reached 190.
According to the applicant, he was examined by a forensic expert in hospital on 18 June 2008.

The forensic report dated 23 June 2008 states that the examination began on 15 June 2008 and ended on 20 June 2008, without specifying the exact date of the applicant's examination by the forensic expert in hospital.

The forensic report of 23 June 2008 recorded that the applicant, Emin Huseynov, stated during the inquiry that on 14 June 2008 a person he did not know had struck him in the neck in Nasimi District Police Station no. 22.

The forensic examination of the applicant was carried out in the resuscitation and intensive care unit of the Clinical Medical Centre of the Baku City Main Health Department in the presence of the lawyer Rashid Hajili.

According to the applicant as recorded in the forensic report, at approximately 12.30 p.m. to 1 p.m. on 14 June 2008 during an event dedicated to the eightieth anniversary of the birth of Che Guevara in café Alaturka, plain clothes persons took him and other attendees to Nasimi District Police Station no. 22.
According to the applicant as recorded in the forensic report, he was struck in his head at the time of being taken from café Alaturka and later at the police station.
The forensic report of 23 June 2008 found that no injuries or objective signs of injury (bruise, abrasion, wound, swelling, etc.) were noticed on the body of the applicant, Emin Huseynov.

The forensic report of 23 June 2008 found that the applicant's medical record no. 5190 from the Clinical Medical Centre of the Baku City Main Health Department showed that at 5.20 p.m. on 14 June 2008 the applicant, aged 29, was admitted to the resuscitation and intensive care unit with the diagnosis of traumatic brain injury and contusion of the soft tissues around the nape of the neck.

The forensic report of 23 June 2008 recorded that the applicant's general state upon admission to hospital was serious, with blood pressure of 190/120 mm Hg and heart pulse of 120 per minute, and that his conscious awareness was impaired to the point of deafness.
The forensic report of 23 June 2008 recorded that no injury was noticed on the applicant's skin upon admission to hospital and that the diagnosis was neurological reaction (nevrotik reaksiya).
The forensic report of 23 June 2008 recorded that on 15 June 2008 there was no pathological change in side projected X-ray examinations of the side and neck vertebras of the cranium of the applicant.

The forensic report of 23 June 2008 recorded that the cerebral computed tomography opinion dated 17 June 2008 found that intraparenchymal traumatic pathological changes were not observed in the applicant, Emin Huseynov.

The forensic report of 23 June 2008 recorded that the computed tomography examination of 17 June 2008 revealed no pathological change in the neck area and no traumatic change in the neck part of the vertebral column of the applicant.
The forensic report of 23 June 2008 recorded that the ultrasound examination of 17 June 2008 revealed no liquid in the abdomen and no hematoma in the parenchymal organs of the applicant.

The forensic report of 23 June 2008 recorded that the applicant's illness was related to extended osteochondrosis of the vertebral column, numerous disc protrusions in the back and neck areas (C 4-5, C 5-6, C 6-7, L 3-4, L 5, S 1), chronic dyscirculatory encephalopathy and vestibulopathy.

The forensic report of 23 June 2008 concluded that the applicant's in-patient treatment was related to his previous diseases — extended osteochondrosis of the vertebral column, numerous disc protrusions in the back and neck areas (C 4-5, C 5-6, C 6-7, L 3-4, L 5, S 1), chronic dyscirculatory encephalopathy and vestibulopathy.
The forensic report of 23 June 2008 was prepared by forensic expert C.A.
The applicant was not provided with a copy of the forensic report dated 23 June 2008.

On 25 June 2008 Nasimi District Police Station no. 22 issued an explanation (arayış) concerning the police intervention of 14 June 2008, signed by the Head of Nasimi District Police Station no. 22, M.T.

The explanation issued by Nasimi District Police Station no. 22 on 25 June 2008 stated that on 14 June 2008, at around 1 p.m., police officers from the Baku City Police Office took measures to identify persons gathered at café 'Alaturka' in the basement of building no. 6 at 28 May Street in Baku, and twenty-two of them were taken to Nasimi District Police Station no. 22.

The explanation issued by Nasimi District Police Station no. 22 on 25 June 2008 stated that after the individuals arrived at Nasimi District Police Station no. 22 at 1.55 p.m., they were registered in the 'apprehended persons' registration log' (gətirilmiş şəxslərin qeydiyyat kitabı) and were released at 4.30 p.m.

The explanation issued by Nasimi District Police Station no. 22 on 25 June 2008 stated that statements were taken from nine of the twenty-two individuals in order to establish the purpose of their gathering.

The explanation issued by Nasimi District Police Station no. 22 on 25 June 2008 stated that the individuals' identity was established and they were released following a 'prophylactic conversation' (profilaktik söhbət).

The explanation issued by Nasimi District Police Station no. 22 on 25 June 2008 stated that Huseynov Emin Rafik oglu, who presented a document stating that he was the chairman of the Institute for Reporters' Freedom and Safety (IRFS), was among the persons apprehended.
By a decision of 27 June 2008, the investigator refused to institute criminal proceedings, finding that there was no evidence that the applicant had been ill-treated by the police.

The investigator's decision of 27 June 2008 noted that the applicant was admitted to the Clinical Medical Centre with the diagnosis of neurological reaction at 5.20 p.m. on 14 June 2008, as established during the examination of the patients' reception log.

The investigator's decision of 27 June 2008 relied on forensic report no. 143/TM of 23 June 2008, which found no injuries or objective signs of injury on the applicant's body and concluded that the applicant's in-patient treatment was related to his previous diseases.
The investigator's decision of 27 June 2008 concluded that no criminal act had been established and that it was appropriate to refuse to institute criminal proceedings.
The applicant was not informed of the decision of 27 June 2008 concerning the investigator's refusal to institute criminal proceedings.
On 16 March 2009 the applicant lodged a criminal complaint with the Nasimi District Court.

In his criminal complaint to the Nasimi District Court, the applicant, relying on Articles 3, 5, 10 and 11 of the Convention, complained that he had been ill-treated by the police during his arrest and whilst in police custody, and that the domestic authorities had failed to conduct an effective investigation in this respect.

In his criminal complaint to the Nasimi District Court, the applicant complained that he had been unlawfully deprived of his liberty and that the police intervention of 14 June 2008 had been unlawful and had constituted an unjustified interference with his rights to freedom of expression and assembly.

In his criminal complaint to the Nasimi District Court, the applicant pointed out that the investigator had questioned neither the police officers who had been involved in the alleged ill-treatment nor the other witnesses.
The applicant stated in his criminal complaint that he had not learned about the existence of the investigator's decision of 27 June 2008 until 3 March 2009.
The applicant stated in his criminal complaint that he had never been provided with a copy of the forensic report dated 23 June 2008.
On 31 March 2009 the Nasimi District Court dismissed the applicant's criminal complaint, finding the investigator's decision of 27 June 2008 lawful.
The Nasimi District Court's decision of 31 March 2009 was silent as to the applicant's particular complaints.
The Nasimi District Court's decision of 31 March 2009 noted that the applicant was admitted to the Clinical Medical Centre with the diagnosis of neurological reaction at 5.20 p.m. on 14 June 2008.

The Nasimi District Court's decision of 31 March 2009 noted that the forensic report found no injuries or objective signs of injury on the applicant's body and that the applicant's in-patient treatment was related to previous diseases he had suffered.

The Nasimi District Court's decision of 31 March 2009 found that the investigator had taken all necessary steps in carrying out a preliminary examination in compliance with Article 207 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and had adopted a justified and lawful decision on refusal to institute criminal proceedings.
On 6 April 2009 the applicant appealed against the Nasimi District Court's decision of 31 March 2009, reiterating his previous complaints.
In his appeal of 6 April 2009, the applicant complained that the investigator had not arranged an identity parade including police officer O.A.

In his appeal of 6 April 2009, the applicant complained that the investigator had not questioned the police officers involved in his arrest and detention, and in particular the Deputy Head of Nasimi District Police Station no. 22 in whose room and in whose presence he had allegedly been ill-treated.
In his appeal of 6 April 2009, the applicant complained that the investigator had failed to obtain video recordings from security cameras situated in Nasimi District Police Station no. 22.
In his appeal of 6 April 2009, the applicant disputed the conclusions of the forensic report dated 23 June 2008, pointing out that he had not been provided with a copy of it.
On 27 April 2009 the Baku Court of Appeal upheld the Nasimi District Court's decision of 31 March 2009.
The applicant lodged a civil action against the Nasimi District Police Office, asking for compensation.

In his civil action against the Nasimi District Police Office, the applicant, relying on Articles 3, 5, 10 and 11 of the Convention, complained that he had been ill-treated by the police, that he had been arrested and taken to the police station unlawfully, and that the police intervention in the gathering had constituted an unlawful interference with his rights to freedom of expression and assembly.
In support of his civil claim, the applicant relied on written eyewitness statements from R.A. and M.H., who stated that police officers had used force against the applicant during his arrest.

R.A. and M.H. stated in their written eyewitness statements submitted in the civil proceedings that when the applicant was in the room of the Deputy Head of Nasimi District Police Station no. 22, they had heard someone shouting at the applicant 'I can eliminate you', 'I can send you to jail'.

R.A. and M.H. stated in their written eyewitness statements submitted in the civil proceedings that when the applicant had been taken out of the room of the Deputy Head of Nasimi District Police Station no. 22, he did not feel well.
On 25 July 2008 the Nasimi District Court refused to admit the applicant's civil action, finding that it did not comply with the procedural requirements for lodging a complaint.
On 2 September 2008 the Baku Court of Appeal upheld the Nasimi District Court's decision of 25 July 2008 refusing to admit the applicant's civil action.
On 17 November 2008 the Supreme Court of Azerbaijan quashed the Baku Court of Appeal's decision of 2 September 2008 and remitted the case to the lower courts for a new examination.
On 17 June 2009 the Nasimi District Court, having examined the applicant's civil action on the merits, decided to dismiss it.
The Nasimi District Court's judgment of 17 June 2009 found that the applicant had been taken to the police station because he had not had his identity card on him.
The Nasimi District Court's judgment of 17 June 2009 found that the police intervention had been lawful, since the gathering at the café in the city centre disturbed other people present.
The Nasimi District Court's judgment of 17 June 2009 found that it had not been established that the applicant had been ill-treated by the police.

The Nasimi District Court's judgment of 17 June 2009 noted that an investigator from Nasimi District Police Station no. 22 had examined the fact that the applicant had sustained injuries and had decided to refuse to institute criminal proceedings because no criminal act had been established, and that this decision had not been challenged.

The Nasimi District Court's judgment of 17 June 2009 found on the basis of witness statements that the applicant had been taken to Nasimi District Police Station no. 22 because he had not had his identity card on him, that he had been detained for a certain period of time, and that he had been released following the establishment of his identity.

The Nasimi District Court's judgment of 17 June 2009 found that the applicant had previously sustained brain injury and regularly underwent medical treatment in Azerbaijan and abroad for a long period of time, and that unexpected health problems had previously been observed in his case.

The Nasimi District Court's judgment of 17 June 2009 found that the fact that the applicant had felt unwell after having been brought to the police station was not related to any duress but to his previous illness.

The Nasimi District Court's judgment of 17 June 2009 found that it was not established that the applicant had sustained a bodily injury or been subjected to physical violence, beaten or been under duress at the police station.
On 3 August 2009 the applicant appealed against the Nasimi District Court's judgment of 17 June 2009, reiterating his previous complaints.
On 14 October 2009 the Baku Court of Appeal dismissed the applicant's appeal against the Nasimi District Court's judgment of 17 June 2009.
On 7 May 2010 the Supreme Court of Azerbaijan upheld the lower courts' judgments in the civil proceedings.
Article 207 of the Code of Criminal Procedure of Azerbaijan provides the rules concerning the examination of information about committed criminal offences by the investigating authorities.

In accordance with Article 207 of the Code of Criminal Procedure of Azerbaijan, an investigator or the prosecutor in charge of the case, after the examination of information about the commission of a criminal offence, should adopt a decision instituting criminal proceedings, refusing to institute criminal proceedings, or transferring the information to the relevant investigating authority or the court in case of private criminal prosecution.

In accordance with Article 212.2 of the Code of Criminal Procedure of Azerbaijan, any person providing information about a committed or planned criminal offence should be provided within twenty-four hours with a copy of the investigator's decision concerning refusal to institute criminal proceedings.
